definition.simple: Mitochondria are the power plants of the cell, making energy from the food we eat.
definition.academic: Double-membrane-bound organelles that generate most of the chemical energy needed to power the cell's biochemical reactions.

examples: Muscle cells have lots of mitochondria because they need a lot of energy to move.

common_misconceptions: Mitochondria create energy from nothing (they actually convert it from food).
Plants don't have mitochondria because they have chloroplasts (they have both).
ai_context.tutor_hint: Ask: 'Where does your phone get its energy? A battery. What is the battery of the cell?'
